claim: The documented direction runs from carnitine depletion to CoA unavailability to mitochondrial impairment, not the reverse
source_value: Single-patient case report (n=1, a 21-month-old girl with B12-unresponsive methylmalonic aciduria). Carnitine increased hippurate excretion, an index of intramitochondrial ATP and CoA availability, raised short-chain urinary acylcarnitines, and reduced methylmalonate and methylcitrate. Carnitine acts by removing propionyl groups, releasing CoA and restoring ATP
note: Added because a draft of Section 5.1 had drawn the arrow the other way, from mitochondrial impairment to degraded carnitine handling. Nothing in the paper now asserts that direction, and Model C no longer needs either. The sample size is n=1 and the text now says so; the source's opening sentence is a general statement about the disorder and does not license a plural claim

claim: The two published PK/PD models of this system use a different structure from (1): the population dose-selection model treats each marker as a turnover state with first-order loss, and the translational model puts the indirect response on the enzyme and makes the markers a direct saturating function of it
source_value: Gao: 'An indirect inhibition Kin model was used to describe the PD response of 3-HP and 2-MC.' Attarwala: 'PCC protein expression rate was modeled as a linear function of plasma PCCA/B mRNA concentration using a 2-compartment indirect response PD model with an empirical effect compartment' and 'PCC protein-mediated reduction of 2-MC, 3-HP, and C3/C2 ratios was modeled using a direct sigmoidal maximum inhibition (Imax) model'
note: Added so the note says how it relates to the prior art it already cites. The two differ from each other at the marker: Gao gives the marker its own turnover equation, Attarwala gives it an algebraic Imax in PCC protein, whose Table 1 carries E0, base, IC50 and a fixed Imax and no biomarker turnover constant at all. Neither is Michaelis-Menten in the marker, which is the point the paragraph makes. Recorded as drift rather than a match for the Gao half: 'whose loss is first order' is the definition of the model class the abstract names, and not something the abstract states, since it carries no PD equations and no biomarker parameters. Same standard as C02 and C03

claim: The smaller Riyadh cohort's authors attribute their own elevated incidence to families with a known metabolic disorder being advised to deliver at the same centre
source_value: 'The increased incidence in our study could be attributed to the family history of a metabolic disorder, with the couples being advised to have their next babies delivered in the same center.'
note: Replaces the false-positive caveat that C10 used to carry. That caveat is real but is raised about biotinidase and the recall rate, not about PA, whose figure rests on confirmed cases; ascertainment is the source's own PA-relevant caveat and is the one that bears on a numerator of four

claim: Propionate oxidation by breath test is near-identical in patients whose serum markers differ widely, and repeats at a CV of 6.9% in controls and, in patients, a mean of 14.0% with a range of 0.4 to 50.8% over n=15
source_value: Test repeatability robust in controls and in MMA subjects (mean coefficient of variation 6.9% and 12.8% respectively), despite widely variable serum methylmalonic acid concentrations in the patients
note: Independent empirical confirmation of the capacity-versus-level conflation this note is about. TWO CAVEATS CARRIED IN THE TEXT. The cohort is methylmalonic acidemia, not propionic acidemia; no published PA breath-test cohort reports repeatability, which is the gap Tier 1 fills. And the DRIFT: the source's abstract calls 12.8% a 'mean coefficient of variation', which the per-subject data do not support. It is the standard deviation of the per-subject coefficients; the mean is 14.02 +/- 12.86%. The paper quotes 14.0% and withdraws 12.8% in both places it appeared, Section 8 and Section 9. The register row previously pointed at sections/00_abstract.tex, where the claim no longer lives

claim: A 50% lower plasma 3-HP is associated with a decompensation rate ratio of 0.7, 95% CI 0.6 to 0.9, p<0.01
source_value: A 50% lower plasma 3-HP concentration was associated with a 30% lower frequency of MDEs (RR 0.7; 95% CI 0.6, 0.9; p < 0.01)
note: The confidence interval is newly verified against the source. The CONDITIONING is the point: the ratio is attached to a LOWER concentration, so RR < 1 means fewer events when the marker is lower. 3-HP is a risk marker in the expected direction, not a protective one; reading RR 0.7 without the conditioning inverts it

claim: The trial measures four markers together: 3-HP, 2-MC, C3 and n-propionylglycine
source_value: Reductions from baseline in disease biomarkers, including 3-HP, 2-MC, propionylcarnitine (C3) and n-propionylglycine, were observed after dose 3 in most patients
note: Cited for the composition of the panel, which is what the multi-output observation model of Remark 15 would be fitted to

claim: C3 is propionylcarnitine, the product of the carnitine conjugation route, so carnitine supplementation raises it while lowering the organic acids
source_value: Urinary excretion of free carnitine decreased while excretion of short-chain acylcarnitines, mostly propionylcarnitine, increased; proposed mechanism is mitochondrial propionylcarnitine formed from free carnitine and excess propionyl-CoA
note: This is the structural ground for excluding C3 as the marker: the selective perturbation of section 3.4 would enter the observation with the wrong sign on that channel

claim: Residual PCC activity in propionic acidemia is under 5% of control, which on the scale the local block fixes puts the disease at theta <= 150
source_value: Each of seven lines from patients with propionic acidemia had clearly detectable PCC activity which was less than 5% of that in control lines
note: The under-5% figure is the source's and is quoted exactly. The DRIFT is the step from it to a capacity: the source is PCC partially purified from cultured fibroblasts, not in vivo hepatic capacity, and its own annotation records that it bears on the 5% vs 10% question without settling it. The 150 is therefore the author's adopted reference of September 2026 applied to the local block's scale, not a measured hepatic capacity, and Section 11 says so. Nothing in the paper's results depends on 5% rather than 10%: the working band's lower edge is 82% of nominal either way

claim: The consensus regimen for cyclical intestinal antibiotics is one to two weeks of metronidazole alternating with two to three weeks off
source_value: '10-20 mg/kg/day divided in 2-3 times... 1-2 weeks of therapy alternating with 2-3 weeks off or alternating every month is advisable.'
note: Cited for the PERIOD of the perturbation, which is what decides whether an unrecorded antibiotic cycle aliases with the sampling interval. The guideline gives a range rather than a schedule, so the paper sweeps three- to five-week periods rather than assuming one

claim: Metronidazole lowers propionate metabolite excretion by a mean of 41%, range 12 to 76%, with plasma propionate falling from 45.0 to 25.1 umol/L, in four PA and five MMA children
source_value: Mean decrease in urinary propionate metabolites 41% (range 12-76, P < 0.01); mean plasma propionate 45.0 -> 25.1 umol/l (P < 0.05), in 5 MMA + 4 PA children
note: Cited for the AMPLITUDE of the same perturbation. The cohort is nine children across two diseases, so the figure sets an order of magnitude and not a per-patient effect; the paper's instruction is to record the weeks, which does not depend on the size

claim: The breath test was first applied in five patients with propionic acidemia among twenty subjects, where recovery was significantly below normal and correlated with clinical severity in PA but not in MMA
source_value: 5 PA, 8 MMA, 1 MCD, 1 TC-II, 5 controls; recovery and half-time in PA significantly below normal, 'well correlated with clinical severity in PA, but did not correlate in MMA'
note: This is the source that makes Tier 1 not an extrapolation from the wrong disease. It reports NO repeatability CV, which is precisely the gap Tier 1 exists to fill, so it narrows the objection rather than removing it

claim: European practice records what patients are prescribed rather than what they eat, and no study in propionic acidemia reports repeated as-eaten intake
source_value: European survey, 186 PA patients / 47 centres / 14 countries; 74% were PRESCRIBED natural protein below WHO/FAO/UNU safe levels; PFAA supplied a median 44% of total protein
note: The first half is the source's and exact: every intake figure it reports is a prescription. The DRIFT is the second half, that no PA study reports repeated as-eaten intake, which is an absence this repository has searched for and not found rather than something the source states. It is the load-bearing half, so it is flagged rather than buried

claim: In the one protein-restricted inborn error where prescribed and actual intake have been compared, actual natural protein ran at 167% of prescribed, a median of 40% above it
source_value: 16 children with PKU, 12-18 one-day diaries and ~22 blood spots each over 6 months. Median prescribed natural protein 6 g/day against an actual 10 g/day: actual = 167% of prescribed, a median +40% (P < 0.001)
note: The disease is PKU and not PA, which the text says. It is cited to show that the gap between prescribed and eaten is large where anyone has measured it, which is what makes the 12% recording requirement of R17 a real risk rather than a hypothetical one

claim: The other published structure, a turnover marker whose production the therapy inhibits, is identifiable in theta at a constant load
source_value: Gao: 'An indirect inhibition Kin model was used to describe the PD response of 3-HP and 2-MC.' Baek: mechanism of action across mRNA-3927, mRNA-3705 and mRNA-3210, with PD responses sustained 3-4 weeks after dosing in Pcca-/- mice
note: The sources are cited for the STRUCTURE of that model, a marker with its own turnover equation, and not for the identifiability conclusion, which is this paper's own analysis of it. Same reading as C46

claim: Published human carnitine kinetics put whole-body turnover at 38 to 119 h, with a rapidly equilibrating compartment at 2 to 3 h, so carnitine is not fast relative to the marker
source_value: Review of L-carnitine kinetics: circulating carnitine distributes to a large slow-turnover compartment (presumably muscle) and a small rapid-turnover one (presumably liver, kidney and other tissues). The two turnover times the paper quotes could not be re-read from here
note: Cited in prose rather than \cite-d until now, which left a load-bearing external figure outside both the bibliography and this register; that is what this row fixes. Recorded as DRIFT and not a match: the compartmental structure is the source's, and the paper's use of it, that carnitine is slower than the marker rather than faster, follows from it either way, but the specific 38-119 h and 2-3 h were carried over from the branch of PR #3 and every registrar and full-text host is denied at this environment's proxy, so they could not be confirmed against the record here. The sentence the paper builds on this is that the reduction needs no separation of timescales, which is argued algebraically in the next paragraph and does not rest on the two figures

claim: Plasma clearance of methylmalonic acid during haemodialysis in a mut0 patient is 103 mL/min at a volume of distribution of 0.48 L/kg, which is the nearest measured analogue for the alternative clearance rate k_e
source_value: A single haemodialysis session led to a 54% reduction in plasma methylmalonic acid and yielded a plasma clearance of 103 mL/min and a VD of 0.48 L/kg, which approximates the total body free water space, followed by rapid reaccumulation to the predialysis concentration over 24 h
note: The two figures are the source's and exact. Recorded as DRIFT because of what the paper does with them, not because of what they say: the clearance is DIALYTIC and not endogenous, so it bounds the endogenous route from above rather than measuring it, and the analyte is methylmalonic acid, which is dicarboxylic with strong tubular handling where 3-HP is monocarboxylic. The row states both caveats and calls the result a plausibility band rather than a substitute. The conversion to a rate constant, 4.41 per day at 70 kg, is this paper's arithmetic on the source's two numbers and not a reported value

claim: 3-hydroxypropionate is already quantified in dried blood spots at the sensitivity a tracer study would need, so the readout for measuring k_e exists
source_value: Second-tier LC-MS/MS assay determining 3-hydroxypropionic acid, methylmalonic acid and methylcitric acid in dried blood spots for newborn screening of propionic acidemia, methylmalonic acidemias and combined remethylation disorders
note: The assay and its analyte are the source's. The DRIFT is the inference: the source establishes that 3-HP can be quantified in dried blood spots for newborn screening, not that its sensitivity suffices for the micro-dose tracer protocol this paper sketches, which is this paper's judgement and is stated as such. The same source is cited in the constants registry for the newborn 99.9th centile, which is a different claim
